newsitem.title: USA: Farmland Industries Inc Q1 net declines.
newsitem.headline: Farmland Industries Inc Q1 net declines.

text.p: Farmland Industries Inc reported net income for its fiscal first quarter, ended November 30, declined to $23.9 million from $52.3 million a year ago. Consolidated sales totalled $2.39 billion, up more than 10 percent over the same 1995 period.
It attributed the decline in net income to a shortened autumn plant nutrient application season, brought on by the early onset of cold weather.

Farmland also cited higher costs for natural gas, higher input prices for the feed division, declining margins in the beef and pork divisions due to higher beef and hog prices, lower volumes of grain movement, and reduced operating margins for grain processing.
The farmer-owned cooperative said the increase in sales was due to higher sales in the petroleum, feed, beef, pork and grain divisions.
"The changes in the market and their impact on fiscal quarterly results were generally anticipated," said President and Chief Executive Officer H.D. Cleberg in a statement.
